utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please be seated. Registrar, please have the accused brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Are the interpreters ready? Does everybody hear? Mr. Blaskic -- first the Prosecutor, do you hear, the Defence? Good morning, everybody. Mr. Blaskic, do you hear me?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLASKIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, good morning, I hear you well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think that we can now resume the cross-examination of Colonel Bryan Watters. Registrar, would you please have the witness brought in so that the cross-examination can continue. Mr. Kehoe?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, can we just go into private session concerning the issue that we ended with yesterday and the representations that were made by the Office of the Prosecutor yesterday afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You do not want us first to finish with the cross-examination? We do not really want to keep disturbing the arrangements we have made. I thought we had gotten to a certain point in the cross-examination, I am not sure we should stop it there. What is your opinion about that, Mr. Hayman?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I am not sure what this is about. Is this about interpreters, your Honour? I do not know clearly what it is that needs to be addressed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: So we can know what subject will be raised, I would ask the Registrar to have a private session set up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Perhaps we could have the witness brought in now then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Colonel Watters, do you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you have a good evening, are you well rested?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We can now resume the cross-examination by General Blaskic's Defence attorney. Mr. Hayman, you have the floor. LIEUTENANT COLONEL WATTERS (continued)

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Colonel Watters.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Just as a preliminary question, in preparing for your testimony, did you have occasion to review any diaries, notes, radio logs, reports, documents of that sort?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Can you tell us first of all, what types of documents did you review?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I reviewed the military information summaries, which were produced by our intelligence cell in 1 Cheshire battle group. I reviewed the daily situation reports, which were produced by the operations room of 1 Cheshire battle group and I reviewed some of the radio logs of the battle group VHF Net.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: And the copies of those documents you reviewed, had they been redacted or cut up, if you will, or were they complete copies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were complete copies.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did your review of those materials help refresh your recollection of the events in question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They enabled me to put my recollections in a sequential order, which was the difficulty I was having, four years later, trying to remember the order in which things happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: So you have relied on them in your testimony here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you remember what period of radio logs you reviewed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The major area of radio logs I reviewed was from 16th April through until about 21st April.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: And Mil Info Summs and daily Sit Rep reports, did you review all of the reports prepared during your tour, that is your personal period of time spent in the theatre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I also did review those areas before I arrived from the point at which our tour started there, which I had known at the time, but after four years had forgotten a great deal of information.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you also have a chance to review any of these materials prior to giving the statements that you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did. We as a battalion hold copies or the originals of those documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you review your statements, one or more of your statements before giving testimony here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Today, no, yesterday, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to ask you a few questions concerning the issue of control of roads in Central Bosnia. Are you familiar with the hill at Grbavica that overlooks the Vitez/Travnik road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am, we call it the mountain road, the road that leads from Dubravica up to Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Actually I am referring to the road from Vitez to Travnik.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I know that road very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Is Grbavica located to the north of that road and to the west north west of the UNPROFOR camp at Bila?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would have to check on the map to be honest, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Could you take a look? I am sorry to have to ask you to rise so soon in your testimony. (Pause). The location is not marked on the Prosecutor's map, your Honour. Did you find it, Colonel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If it is the hill that was behind our base in Stari Bila, then I know that hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: And adjacent to -- could you tell us in terms of direction where the hill is located from your camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was just to the east of our camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Very well. Would you agree that that hill dominated the road, the road from Vitez to Travnik at that point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that point, yes it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Would you agree that that road from Vitez to Travnik was a road of strategic military significance to both the HVO and the Army of BiH?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: When you arrived in the theatre, were you briefed concerning any efforts of the Army of BiH to control that position on the hill at Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw no evidence routinely that anyone was controlling that hill. We actually used to control that hill ourselves when we were, for example, bringing in helicopters to evacuate our wounded, because the hill had a strategic domination over the local countryside. I do not remember seeing BiH positions on that hill, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: If I could ask the usher to assist in placing a document before the witness, I believe the usher may have stepped out, I can do it, your Honour, with your leave. (Handed). Your Honour, this is a four page document, parts of it were redacted prior to being provided to the Defence and the page I am interested in for today's purposes is the last. I will read it all if the Prosecutor so wishes, otherwise I suggest we hold the first three pages in abeyance, if you will, and concentrate on the fourth page. If the ELMO could be activated and the top of the first page could be placed on the ELMO? I would direct your attention, Colonel, to the top of the first page of the document, the handwritten portion which reads: "Cheshire Mil Info 090 29 January 93." Then if the document could be turned to the last and fourth page, thank you Colonel, I will read it: "BiH troops continue to build a number of Defence positions on the Grbavica Brdo feature GR 2099954, which overlooks Bila school. Comment. This feature dominates the main Travnik to Vitez road." First of all, would you agree that this document, although redacted, appears in the format of Mil Info Summs prepared by your regiment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Would you agree that this reference on the fourth page refers to the hill at Grbavica adjacent to the Bila school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you ever have occasion to see these defensive positions referred to in the Mil Info Summ?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Mil Info Summ was dated before I arrived and was the -- reflected the period of the fighting that largely took place in the Kiseljak valley around Busovaca, if my memory serves me. There was no fighting, to the best of my knowledge, of any consequence, around Bila school at that time. Also I think, sir, I ought to put Mil Info Summs into context so that the comment, for example, is relevant. The Mil Info Summs were a daily correlation of all the information that we gained through our patrolling and contact with the local population. They were put together by a captain, a sergeant and a corporal in our intelligence cell and the comment refers to a comment by either the captain or the sergeant as to the relevance of the particular information. The reliability of the information was normally catalogued with an introduction of either a source, meaning a source of information that cannot be substantiated; a normally reliable source, which would mean in the past, when cross-referenced, this information was relevant and accurate, or a reliable source, which meant that repeatedly when cross-referenced the information from this source, which might be one of our own officers, for example, was found to be accurate. They were not designed to be read in single sound bites. You really need to read each daily summary, because each area may reflect and contradict each other, so they do not actually represent necessarily a factual account, they represent the account as we saw it on that day, and very often --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please slow down?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry. The comment and the actual contents of Mil Info Summs were often found to be erroneous when cross-referenced later in further Mil Info Summs with additional information. I am not saying that this particular extract is not accurate, I just wanted to set Mil Info Summs in context; they are not an authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you. I take it you would agree with the comment on this page that this hill or feature dominates the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It dominates the road at that point. It does not dominate the whole road.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I take it from your comment of a moment ago that because, for example, this Mil Info Summ has been so heavily redacted, it is difficult to determine the actual meaning and significance of the document itself, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would need to read the whole Mil Info Summ to get a feel for what the situation was on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: As would anyone, correct, anyone reviewing the Mil Info Summ and trying to draw useful information from it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Mil Info Summs were produced for the command team of 1 Cheshire by the intelligence cell in debriefing patrols and other people we spoke with. The only other people in receipt of them were headquarters UN in Kiseljak and they received them for information as well. They were a tool for the command group of 1 Cheshire to review from an information perspective the events of the day and cross-reference it with events on other days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I have been told that the speed, question/answer, is going too fast and that it is difficult for the transcript -- the court stenographers are having trouble as well, not only interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: We will work harder at it your Honour, thank you. I will review the rest of the Mil Info Summ with the witness if necessary, but first I would like to offer it, having reviewed it to the extent I have.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: May I just, in answering your question, which I never properly did, I am sorry? When I arrived in Vitez school, there was evidence of old defence positions on that hill. They were not occupied at the time that I was in Vitez school and the only time the position was used was during the period about 16 to 25 April, when mortars were placed on and around that feature and fired out and incoming mortar rounds which hit our school as well as that feature came in. We were never quite sure who fired the mortars.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: But there were incoming mortars to the Grbavica hill during the period that included April 16th, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is, but there was nobody on the hill, it was rather a waste of mortars.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I offer the document, your Honour, in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, is counsel offering the entire document including that which he has not discussed?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I will offer it all and if there is an objection perhaps I will offer part.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That is fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I offer all of it at this point, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I was merely asking by way of clarification. That is fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You are asking for the entire document to be put in to the record, is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I would like to remind you -- I am not really sure where we are here, I have kind of lost the thread here, but the question of knowing whether we are putting the entire document when only one part of it has been discussed is a question we have to resolve, but I see since there is no disagreement, we will take the whole document. All right, we will accept the entire document. Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be D62, which is the transparency which is on the easel.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You spoke yesterday at times of refugees.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Are you familiar with refugees from the region of the Krajina coming to the Lasva Valley?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not particularly, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: During your tour, did you hear of the 1st Krajina Brigade of the Army of BiH?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At this time I do not have a recollection of that, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you hear of the 7th or 27th Krajina Brigade during your tour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was familiar with the fall of the Krajina, but I was not familiar and have no direct recollection of individual brigades.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Would that include the 305th Jajce Brigade, also part of the Krajina brigades?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do remember a Jajce brigade, that was an external brigade located in Gornji Vakuf and its presence was very disruptive. I remember we assisted the removal of that brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: It was disruptive in the sense that they were outside forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Within the efforts of BritBat to establish a cease-fire in Gornji Vakuf, one of the HVO objections was to the presence of the Jajce Brigade, which they believed had changed the balance of power within Gornji Vakuf and wanted that, as they described it, "external brigade" moved out of the environment of Gornji Vakuf, where its presence in HVO terms was preventative of them agreeing to a cease-fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: During your tour, did you learn whether the reserve headquarters of the third corpus was in Preocica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Yesterday at times you spoke of a Muslim minority in the Lasva Valley. Was the population mix in the Lasva Valley prior to the conflict in 1993 approximately 50/50, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry, I would not know that. I suspect it might have been. I do not know and you would have to define the Lasva Valley as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Yesterday you spoke of mortars.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Would you agree that certain mortars are under the control of an artillery unit or group, while other mortars are infantry mortars?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: What size mortars would be controlled by infantry?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is quite difficult. I would suspect that anything below 60 millimetres might be controlled by infantry, and that is certainly the case in the British army. Anything above 60 to 80 millimetres would be classified as an artillery piece and would be controlled by artillery units.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: So 60 to 80 millimetres you believe is a range which could fall either way, either to infantry forces or to an artillery unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, certainly in the British army.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you know about the former JNA, where those mortars would fall in terms of command and authority?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would suspect in the JNA it was probably quite similar to the British army.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: What about RPGs, rocket propelled grenades? Would they typically be held and controlled by infantry units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I saw those being carried by infantry units of BiH and HVO in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You spoke yesterday of Mr. Kordic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Can you give us an example of an occasion when Colonel Blaskic was not able to deal with a problem and as a result you went to Mr. Kordic for action?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can. There was a convoy coming from the direction of a central aid depot in Zenica, bound for Travnik. The convoy was stopped by a checkpoint close to the Busovaca/Vitez road junction. The young officer commanding the convoy failed to execute his halt convoy drills properly, in that he did not slew his Warrior to block the forward movement of the convoy. He had anti-tank mines placed by HVO soldiers at the front and rear of the tracks of his Warrior, so blocking his Warrior in position, and the troops climbed on -- the HVO troops climbed on to the running board of the lead vehicle, put a rifle through the side window, injuring the driver, and ordered him at gunpoint to drive round the Warrior, and this happened simultaneously down the convoy. Those vehicles were taken, turning left, down to Busovaca and left into a factory complex on the north side of Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: So the convoy was hijacked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is the description of the hijack. The officer commanding the convoy said to the commander of the HVO soldiers doing this, "this convoy has got the authority of the regional commander HVO, Colonel Tihomir Blaskic, to move safely through this area", and the commander said, "we do not take our orders from Blaskic, we take our orders from Kordic".

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: The individual who said this, were they in an uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: What kind of uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again, I was not there, the description was they were in black uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Were they described to you as HVO soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We described everybody as HVO soldiers who were Croat. We were aware there were other HVO units, HOS types, who dressed slightly different from normal HVO soldiers, but to keep things simple for our junior commanders we referred to Muslims as BiH and Croats as HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: The information you received on this particular occasion was that the HVO troops were dressed in black?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Let me direct your attention now to 16th April. On that occasion, that morning, you drove into Vitez, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You saw certain dead bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You saw some of those bodies in a portion of Vitez that you would characterise as the Muslim portion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: And did you also see five bodies in what you believe to be the Croat portion of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not quite sure what the -- those five bodies were beyond Vitez, although within the environs of Vitez. They were over the bridge on the far side of the town, turn right and they were on the left. I would not know what the specific ethnic mix of that was. They were certainly outside of the two defined areas we knew as Muslim and Croat, so I would not be able to comment. I certainly could not tell from the state of the bodies whether they were Croats or Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: On that morning, you went into Stari Vitez and met with Sefkija Djidic, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: What did he say to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was confused as to what the situation was, he was fighting a defensive battle and was keen to see a cease-fire and was willing to personally come to Vitez school to discuss a cease-fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Were there soldiers at his headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Actually now I reflect on it, it is slightly strange. There were very few soldiers actually in his headquarters. I suspected they were manning positions on the Muslim edge of the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: How many did you see at his headquarters in Stari Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not very many. I really cannot remember. Two or three, something like that, four.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Were they armed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: What kind of arms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: AK 47s?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: AK 47 generic weapons, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: And Djidic made clear to you that he was defending the town, Stari Vitez, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did he tell you that so far he had successfully defended the town against the HVO attack?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You know from your own knowledge that that defence was successful throughout the day of 16th April, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: The 17th April, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: And on to the end of your tour in May 1993, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You also visited the Hotel Vitez on the morning of 16th April 1993, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember, I do not think I did. I may have done and then, not being able to find who I needed to talk to, I went to a cinema building around the back of Vitez, which was the headquarters of HVO Vitez, as opposed to the Hotel Vitez, which was the headquarters of regional command Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you at least drive by the Hotel Vitez on the morning of 16th April?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Outside of the Hotel Vitez, did you see HVO soldiers taking up armed positions with their firearms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Were they aiming in the direction of Stari Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Would you agree that as of 16th April 1993 Stari Vitez posed a military threat to the Hotel Vitez, the headquarters of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What do you mean by "military threat"?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Could snipers in Stari Vitez attack, hit, fire upon the Hotel Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they could.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: And in fact later in the day on the 16th, you met with two HVO soldiers, Mr. Prskalo and Mr. Pilisic, correct, in this meeting at 12.30?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: After the meeting they returned, you were informed, to the Hotel Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were taken back by the liaison officer responsible for Vitez/Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You were later informed they were both hit by sniper on the afternoon of the 16th after exiting an UN Warrior on their way walking towards the Hotel Vitez, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Is there any doubt in your mind that that fire came from Stari Vitez, which hit those two men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know the exact positions of the sniper fire, but they were certainly Muslim snipers. The direction of fire the liaison officer believed was from his rear as he was walking towards the hotel, which would be in the direction of Stari Vitez. I cannot be specific as to where the sniper positions were. We did not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: As you drove by the Hotel Vitez that morning, could you see whether the windows had been shot out or broken out by grenades?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not have a memory of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you recall, did you go in the building, the Hotel Vitez, or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I did. It is really difficult to remember exactly what I did on that morning in detail. I have a vivid memory of going to the cinema and I have a vague memory of going into the Hotel Vitez. Whether it was on the morning of the 16th, the afternoon of the 16th, whether it was on the 17th or 18th I cannot remember, I am afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I understand. On your way in and out of Stari Vitez on the morning of 16th April 1993, did you see any trenches or earthen fortifications around the perimeter of Stari Vitez, the Muslim portion of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not have a recollection of that, no. I suspected people were defending the positions from the houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Would that be normal in the absence of earthen fortifications, that any available structure would be used to mount a defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Later on in your tour, sniping from Stari Vitez continued to be a problem and an issue, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sniping from both directions in Vitez, from Vitez centre into Stari Vitez and from Stari Vitez into central Vitez was a problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you know during the period of your service in Bosnia how many dead and wounded in Vitez were sustained as a result of sniper fire from Stari Vitez directed against Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you know who may have gathered those statistics or kept records of those dead and wounded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Mil Info Summs will have reflected what we were told by various sources and that would probably have been from the commander of Vitez HVO forces to our liaison officer in contact. I suspect that information would be in Mil Info Summs. The accuracy of that information -- I would have to read the Mil Info Summs to gain an impression of how accurate that impression might be.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Would you also agree that mortars and RPGs fired from within Stari Vitez could threaten the entire geographic area of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Now let me turn your attention to your visit to Kruscica later in the day on 16th April 1993. Kruscica lies directly to the south, or below, on the map which is Exhibit 29J, below Vitez, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct, south of Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You went there around 5.30 in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you determine as a result of your visit that the Army of BiH may have been firing mortars from Kruscica into Vitez on 16th April?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there was nothing to indicate that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Have you said that in any prior interview with the Office of the Prosecutor, that the Armija could have been firing mortars from Kruscica on 16th April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was not the question you asked me. Did I see evidence? The answer was I did not see evidence, but certainly there were BiH positions there and certainly Vitez would be in range of mortars in Kruscica.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Was part of the discussion between the United Nations forces and the Army of BiH prior to your going to Kruscica a request by the United Nations that the Army of BiH stop its attack on Poculica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Are you talking about the conference at 12.30?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I am referring to the discussions and the conditions that were set forth by the Army of BiH in which one of their demands was that UNPROFOR come to Kruscica and evacuate what the Army of BiH described as "wounded female civilians".

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was one of the conditions, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: What is that UNPROFOR wanted the Armija to do, that this was a condition precedent for stated by the Armija?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We just wanted them to stop all indirect fire and fighting within the environs of Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did that include fighting in the area of Poculica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It included fighting everywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Including Poculica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It would include Poculica. Fighting everywhere, no specifics.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: After you got to Kruscica, did you find that virtually all of the injured were men, not women?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that is the case. They were certainly men and women, they were not just women, which was what we understood they were. There were women among them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: But it was predominantly male casualties correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct. I think there were only about five or six, and I think three out of the five or six were male.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: How many Army of BiH soldiers did you see at the BiH headquarters in Kruscica on the afternoon of 16th April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Half a dozen, a dozen.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you see other soldiers of the Army of BiH in trenches or other earthen fortifications in Kruscica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not. It was dark when we were driving through.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Again, as in the case with Stari Vitez, would you believe that in fact the soldiers of BiH at the time were predominantly dispersed in defensive positions, not congregated at the headquarters in Kruscica at the time you visited?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Lacking trenches, would you also believe it to be true that they were using any and all available structures in Kruscica to mount their defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did Kruscica fall to the HVO on 16th April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did it fall on the 17th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did it fall at any time prior to your leaving the theatre on May 8th 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: So we can say, can we not, that the Army of BiH successfully defended Kruscica from the HVO attack that began on 167th April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but on that night my view of the position was that they actually were going to lose. I was quite surprised they managed to defend it. We went back the next morning to try and see, and our route back was blocked by anti-tank mines and a bowser across the road which we managed to negotiate. We got back to the BiH headquarters and they were still defending the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: So it was a pitched battle which you witnessed on the late afternoon/evening of 16th April in Kruscica, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw very -- I have no recollection of seeing anything leaving Kruscica in terms of artillery or mortars and a vivid recollection of an enormous amount of RPG, mortar and artillery coming into Kruscica. I described it as being in a bowl, it just looked like a cauldron of fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Kruscica, I believe you said yesterday, lies on a road that could potentially have been used to link Vitez to points south in Herzegovina, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: In that sense, do you agree Kruscica was a location of strategic military significance to both the HVO and the Army of BiH?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would say it is operationally important. I would not say it is strategically important.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Would you agree Kruscica could be used to mortar or shell the town of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was in range of Vitez, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did it mortar or shell Vitez during the course of your tour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It may well have done. Again, I would have to go and check our Mil Info Summs and read them. There is no reason why it did not, but I do not have a vivid recollection of reading about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: If the usher could place a very short document before the witness, your Honour? (Handed). If this could be placed on the ELMO, Mr. President, Colonel Watters, this again is a redacted portion of a document. Let me read it to you: "1. PWO Mil Info Summ number 098 dated 4 July 1993. Vitez. "2. The customary friction between Stari Vitez, Kruscica and the Croat-controlled parts of the town continued with the BiH in Kruscica admitting responsibility for the mortar atk" -- is that "attack"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Yesterday, "yest", is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: "For the mortar attack yesterday which injured 5 times Croats." Would that mean five Croats?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it would.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Can you tell us what PWO refers to in this Mil Info Summ?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it refers to the 1st Battalion of the Prince of Wales' Own Regiment of Yorkshire, who had replaced BritBat 1 Cheshire in mid May, and this Mil Info Summ is dated 4th July and so would refer to a mortar attack which took place on 3rd July.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: After you departed the theatre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two months after we departed the theatre.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Does this document appear to be in the format, to the extent it has not been redacted, of a Mil Info Summ prepared by the military of the United Kingdom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was prepared by the intelligence cell of 1 PWO, I would suspect.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I offer the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would object to this document. This is not a document the facts of which this particular witness knows anything about. This witness left the theatre, I believe it was in and around 11th May 1993, and it may well be some Prince of Wales' own regiment of Yorkshire witnesses that will testify. With all due respect, this particular document should be enquired at at that time. This witness has no knowledge as to the facts concerning this particular document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, the witness -- this dispute over the identification of documents I find to be rather sterile. We have asked Colonel Watters whether it has elements allowing him to identify this type of document. It need not necessarily be a document he himself saw, he was not there on 4th July, but could he still identify this document, or is it a document that reminds him of nothing? The Colonel has seen documents of this kind throughout his career and particularly during the 90 days he was there, so I am addressing myself to the Colonel and ask him whether he can identify this document or not at all.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, it is in the format of the Mil Info Summs that we produced during our time and that the 1 PWO cell produced on our behalf during the changeover period. As to the facts of the case, I obviously cannot comment, or the facts of the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. I propose that we admit it into evidence, registering the reservations made by the witness and the Prosecutor. This document has not been formally identified by the witness, it is a document published in July 1993, and the judges will assess the weight of this document. We are admitting it with the reservations made by the Prosecutor and the witness, so what is the number of this document?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is exhibit D63.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: So admit D63 with the reservations on the part of the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: And the Trial Chamber will evaluate it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Colonel Watters, let me turn your attention to 17th April 1993. You told us yesterday that you went to a war clinic in Vitez and you saw two bodies inside the clinic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct. On the visit to Kruscica, the commander in Kruscica had no medical resources or personnel and the two doctors who administered Kruscica from the clinic in Vitez had not returned back to the village of Kruscica where they lived, and he asked if we would enquire through the officers of the HVO whether they could locate these two doctors, and whether we could get reassurance to the BiH commander in Kruscica as to their safety, and he wished them to be returned back to that village.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: So did you go to the clinic and enquire as to the whereabouts and safety of these two doctors?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We went first of all to the headquarters of Vitez town, to Mario Cerkez's headquarters. They did not know about the whereabouts of any doctors, but were able to show us on our maps where the clinic was within the town. We informed them that we would go to the clinic and see if we could find the doctors.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did they tell you who controlled the clinic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: They did not mention the name Kraljevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have no recollection of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: So you went to the clinic. Did you enquire as to the safety and whereabouts of these two doctors at the clinic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was nobody at the clinic. The area was under sniper fire and there was nobody around.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Sniper fire from where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is very difficult to tell where you are being fired at from snipers. All you actually hear, in an urban environment, is the crack of the round passing by you. It is very difficult to hear the thump which is the actual sound of the rifle firing. We were quite disorientated as to where the sniper fire was coming from.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Was the clinic in a location such that it was exposed to potential sniper fire from Stari Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it probably was. I would have to look at an air photograph and try and reorientate myself, I am afraid. It is not something I have thought about.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Were you given the names of the doctors you were enquiring about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: What were the names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: After you went to the clinic and found it under assault --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was under sniper fire, not assault.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Under sniper fire, did you undertake any other enquiry to try and determine the safety and whereabouts of these two doctors?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We looked through the windows, went right round the clinic. In the clinic there were two men dressed in white coats lying dead. There was nobody else in the clinic, there was nobody we could enquire from. We went back and told the HVO headquarters that we could not locate the doctors, we had found two men in the clinic in white coats, they may well have been the doctors, and that was as far as I proceeded with that enquiry, although I was aware that the BiH pursued the enquiry further. I am not totally clear as to where it went.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My assumption was that the two men in the clinic were the two dead doctors.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Other than your visual observations, did you ever confirm or disprove that these doctors had been harmed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember the doctors ever reappearing, but as I say, the issue was subsumed by far more important issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You did not go to Zenica to look for them, I take it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Would the names of these doctors be located in any records, reports, radio logs or other papers in the possession of UNPROFOR or 1 Cheshire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They might be, they may well be in a Mil Info Summ. I do not have a recollection of their names, I just remember referring to them as "the two doctors".

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Let me turn your attention to 19th April. You discussed yesterday coming upon a group of, I believe, women and children blocking the road --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And some old men.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, blocking the road between Vitez and Busovaca around the Nadioci area, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not between Vitez and Busovaca, it was beyond that junction towards the Zenica flyover.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: So above the Kaonik junction towards Zenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think so. Again, I would have to check the map. I think that is roughly where they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: If Exhibit 53B could be retrieved, your Honour, it was shown to the witness yesterday.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When you say the Vitez road, I think of the road from Kaonik down to Busovaca, it was not on that road. It was on the road from Vitez to the Zenica flyover.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Was it near the so-called Swiss chalet building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: That is in the area of Nadioci, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Would you go more slowly, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: My apologies. Do you know who occupied the Swiss chalet at this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My recollection is describing them as a HOS-type unit. We may have been able to identify them in our Mil Info Summs. I do not remember the exact detail of them, but they did certainly seem to keep themselves to themselves within that military base.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You spoke to an individual who held himself out to be a commander, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you know who that was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know his name. He would not give his name, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you know his rank?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not recollect his rank. He was about six foot two or six foot three, had very fair hair and was athletically built.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Based on the number of soldiers he was directing, can you estimate whether he commanded a platoon or a company or a unit of ten men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not have a recollection of what rank he was and how many soldiers he controlled.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I take it you cannot tell us who his superior commander was, his immediate superior commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I cannot.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: On 22nd April 1993, you went to Jelinak and then you went into Ahmici, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Prior to your visit on 22nd, had you received reports on the 16th April 1993 concerning your units, that is UNPROFOR Warriors visiting Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I had. Ahmici one of many villages, Santici and villages up that side of the Lasva Valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you remember how many Warriors visited Ahmici on 16th April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The exact number of Warriors, no, I do not. It is not something I would focus on. I would know that several different call signs had visited it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Which would mean several different vehicles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, several different groups of vehicles, or the same group of vehicles several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: So perhaps nine or ten Warriors, either different or the same Warriors, visited Ahmici at different times on 16th April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Warriors travel in groups of four or groups of two and a call sign was four Warriors. I do not have a recollection of how many Warriors visited, but I certainly know that several call signs visited. Whether all the Warriors turned into Ahmici or not, I do not know the exact detail of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you remember what report you received during 16th April 1993 from the Warriors that visited Ahmici concerning civilian casualties in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were certainly civilian casualties in Ahmici. I have a recollection of one of our Warriors actually removing women and children from Ahmici who were under fire on the 16th, or the environs of Ahmici, in a closed down Warrior. It is quite difficult to work out exactly where you are, just roads within a village complex. Certainly reports of heavy fighting, considerable destruction and casualties, yes, I recollect that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you remember how many civilian casualties were reported to you by the Warriors that visited Ahmici on 16th April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As specific to Ahmici, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: It is not something that sticks in your mind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were reports of casualties all up the Lasva Valley, and the figure at that time, by mid morning, we were very reticent to actually state how many casualties there were, because the reports of soldiers coming in were repeating the casualties seen by the road and there was a danger we were going to multiply the number of casualties. It was one of the reasons why I myself went out. I think we put a figure on the 16th of 30 to 50 or 50 to 100, I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: In the entire Lasva Valley?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: That is dead and wounded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they were bodies, not wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Dead?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Were you told by your units that visited Ahmici on the 16th when the fighting began in Ahmici on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The fighting was happening on the morning of the 16th and it appeared that a great deal of destruction within the village had already taken place.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Were you told by your units when the fighting ended in Ahmici on 16th April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not have a recollection of that. There was no reason on the 16th to specifically focus on Ahmici. At that time Ahmici was, to our knowledge, no worse than Santici or any of the other villages up the Lasva Valley. Vitez was actually the area of most interest.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: While I am asking the next few questions, your Honour, I would ask that the Registrar assist by putting up what is a map or aerial photograph of Ahmici and should be at hand. I believe it is 53 -- no, Exhibit 50. You described for us yesterday visiting Ahmici and identified a number of photographs taken at three different houses that you visited. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do. That was on 22nd April.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Yes, on 22nd April. If you could look at Exhibit 50 with me and tell us whether you can identify the three houses that you visited.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Go ahead, Mr. Kehoe, if you like.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo is retrieving an overhead transparency, your Honour, in case the witness is able to identify the specific houses. Using Exhibit 50, Colonel, can you identify the first house that you visited?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is very difficult. It was in this area here (indicates).

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Could you stand to the side slightly so the court can see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was in this area here. I am afraid at this time I am unable to accurately point at it. If I was to guess I would think it was one of the houses here on the right-hand side, but I cannot exactly point out the house. We did not use air photographs, we just used maps that did not show the individual houses on that morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: But I take it there is an area within which you can definitively say the house was located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said I am guessing, it was in the upper part of the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Are you able to say with any more specificity, other than the upper half or part of the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I said, I would be guessing if I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Which house was this, was this the house with the line of bodies or skeletons in the basement, or one of the other two houses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first house was the one with the largest number of bodies, the one with the skull I think was in the lower part of the village, but again it was a very short visit to the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Are you able to identify the other two houses you visited? You have identified to the best of your ability the one with the line of corpses or skeletons in the cellar; are you able to identify the other two houses with any greater specificity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, you may be seated. I may have asked you to sit down prematurely. You said that on your visit on 22nd April to Ahmici, you found certain locations where the grass had been matted or tramped down and there were shell casings nearby?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was in the lower part of the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Can you identify that location? I am sorry to ask you to hop up and down, my apologies.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again, I would not be able to do it with accuracy. There were sniper positions in this area here covering the road into Ahmici and we were shot at from there on that morning and in the afternoon. We got out about here (indicates) and we foot-patrolled up here with the Warriors coming behind us giving us cover.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Indicating towards what is marked as the upper mosque Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I think the positions we identified were in the area where we dismounted from our Warriors, so at a guess I would talk around here (indicates). Again, I am afraid four years later to point on a photograph is very difficult, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: We understand it is very difficult, but I take it your best evidence is that the areas with matted down or tramped down grass containing numerous shell casings was in the middle portion of Ahmici where you believe you disembarked from your Warriors, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is as best as my memory serves. I might be wrong but that is what I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: To make it clear for purposes of the record, the middle portion you are indicating is the area adjacent to the large white area, it could be paved, it could be dirt, white area approximately halfway up the Ahmici road on Exhibit 50, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As west as I remember it sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, you may sit down. Let me direct your attention forward in time to April 24th. Did you learn of a meeting on that day in the Hotel Vitez between Colonel Stewart, Ambassador Thebault and Colonel Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were several meetings, I do not have an immediate recollection of that particular one, I am afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Were you briefed by Colonel Stewart or anyone else concerning discussions at that meeting regarding whether a joint commission should be formed, a multi-ethnic joint commission, including international organisations, to investigate the events in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We already had a joint commission, I am trying to disentangle that from other thoughts. I do not remember a joint commission for that purpose ever manifesting itself, and I do not have specific memories of Colonel Stewart discussing that with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: The UNPROFOR force, together with other international organisations, had, would you agree, gathered and was gathering a certain amount of information from victims and survivors of Ahmici, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Certainly the Red Cross was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you discuss with Colonel Stewart whether that information should be shared with the HVO to facilitate their investigation of what happened in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The ICRC would not share that information with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: To your knowledge, they would also not share that information with the HVO, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would not think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: So to your knowledge, the HVO was never given any information derived from the victims and survivors of Ahmici from which they could build and further their own investigation, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That I would think would be correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I am going into a new area, your Honour. I am happy to continue, but I would just advise the court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You can go on until 11.20.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you. On 17th April 1993, do you recall receiving reports that the Army of BiH was advancing from Kuber mountain towards the Croat enclave, the Vitez/Busovaca enclave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have a memory of that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: If the usher could assist, your Honour? I would ask that this document be placed on the ELMO before the witness, it is short.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Excuse me, Colonel Watters, I would not like that there be any more incidents about identifying of documents. Are you able to identify this document, to talk about what is on it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is in the format of our documents, sir. It is not a whole document, but it is in the format of our documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: So from the point of view of form, at least theoretically, unless there are any other conditions you would like to make, you do identify this. All right, go ahead, Mr. Hayman.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Before I go further, is this a document that appears to have been created during your tour in Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that would appear to be one of our documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: The top handwritten line reads, "Cheshire Mil Info 169 17 April 93". The body of the document, that which has not been redacted, reads: "I. 12.40 hours. The mayor of Vitez claimed that the Croat village of Poculica, grid reference 2794, had been attacked, resulting 1 HVO soldier and two civilians being badly injured. "J. 13.06 hours. It was reported that the village Donje Veceriska, grid reference 2092, was under attack from the HVO. "K. 13.56 hours. It was reported that the village of Kuber, grid reference 3094 (Croat), was under attack from BiH forces." Is this Mil Info Summ, Colonel, consistent with your recollection of the reports you were receiving on 17th April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I offer the document, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Registrar, this will be exhibit D64 and no conditions attached to it. I think we can now take our break, Mr. Hayman, unless you have any other questions on this specific document? We will resume at 11.40.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We can now resume the hearing. Have the accused brought in now please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Your Honour, I have three additional short Mil Info Summ excerpts that I would ask be placed before the witness and provided to your Honours and the Prosecution. Colonel Watters, if you could take the first one, with the usher's assistance, 19th April 1993, and we will put that on the ELMO. At the top of the document, "Cheshire Mil Info 171 19 April 93". Now moving on the body, paragraph F: "11.06 hours. Colonel Blaskic, HVO Central Bosnia, claimed that there had been a BiH offensive on the area to the north of Busovaca, contravening the cease-fire agreement." First, Colonel, do you agree that reference would be to the cease-fire agreement that was the subject of a Mil Info Summ that you saw yesterday during your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was reference to a HVO cease-fire agreement which we never actually saw ratified by the BiH. It appeared to be a HVO initiative at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You think it was an offer that was never accepted by the BiH?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We never saw any evidence of the BiH accepting that on the ground, and other Mil Info Summs of the same time, we did not actually see it in place within the HVO on the ground either. It was a rather spurious document in our view.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you know whether the BiH representatives ever signed that cease-fire agreement of 18th April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I never saw a copy of that, I only saw a copy of the agreement signed by Colonel Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you have a belief one way or the other?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I really did not know. There was a rumour that a cease-fire had been agreed on the 18th by Mr. Izetbegovic and Mr. Boban, and the first evidence that that might be the case we saw was the HVO document that was in the Mil Info Summ you showed me yesterday. There were negotiations with Colonel Stewart with Mr. Hadzihasanovic and Colonel Blaskic, but none of those negotiations ever manifested anything on the ground. From our view, they were just becoming meaningless and it was not until General Morien on the 20th had a meeting with Colonel Blaskic and Mr. Hadzihasanovic in Zenica, from that followed the conference on the 21st that any will on either side appeared to manifest itself on the ground for a cease-fire, although the HVO were manifestly keen for a cease-fire from about the 18th, as at that point they had achieved their objectives.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Let us return to the text and I read from it: "The attack was reported to be centred on the villages of Kuber, grid reference 29993, Jelinak, grid reference 3092, and Kaonik, grid reference 302903." Is that report, did you find that report to be consistent with other information and other reports you were receiving at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that was during the offensive by the BiH. Whether they had actually achieved those objectives at that time I cannot comment on, but it would be consistent with the fact that there was a BiH counter-offensive during the 19th.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Turning to the second page, please, there is a short paragraph I will read as well, which begins: "2002. It is interesting to note that the hospital which is guarded by HVO soldiers has been clearing both Croat and Muslim casualties. Muslim casualties have also been allowed to be evacuated to the hospital in Travnik by UN call signs." Do you take this to mean, first of all, that Muslim casualties, soldiers from the battlefield as well as civilians, were being evacuated to the so-called Croat hospital at Nova Bila, is that your understanding of the first sentence of this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would guess it is, because the Croat hospital or HVO hospital was in Nova Bila. I have no way of knowing if this refers to it, but that was the main hospital for HVO forces in the Vitez area.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Was it the only hospital in the Vitez/Busovaca enclave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Hospital, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Then the second sentence, would that refer to the evacuation, or appear to refer to the evacuation across the frontlines from Nova Bila to Travnik hospital of Muslim casualties?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it would. Could you put it in context, please? What date was this?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: The Mil Info Summ is dated 19th April 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is part of the same Mil Info Summ.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: It was provided to the Defence as part of the same document, yes. Is that consistent with the reports that you received at the time that the Croat hospital in Nova Bila was assisting wounded, regardless of ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have to confess, it certainly was not a feeling of mine. We evacuated Croat casualties to Nova Bila and we evacuated Muslim casualties to Travnik and both parties agreed to our assistance in moving casualties. I do not know the origin of the report that there were Muslim casualties in the hospital. It is not something I have a memory of, I have to be honest. It could have happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you have any information that would cause you to doubt the report on page 2 of this document, the Mil Info Summ, 19th April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: If you could turn to the next document, please, perhaps with the assistance of the usher. This document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Do you want these to be entered into the record?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I did. I was going to address all three at once, your Honour, but we can do them one at a time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Does the Office of the Prosecutor have any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: No reservations, no objections, so these will be 65 and 66?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, 65 and 66.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Go ahead, Mr. Hayman.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Directing your attention to what has been marked as exhibit D66, it begins at the top in handwritten notation: "Cheshire Mil Info 174 22 April 93. "1. Vitez. The town of Vitez and its surrounding villages were reported to be generally quiet, with the exception of the villages of Sadavace, grid reference 2196 and Brdo, grid reference 2297. Recce", is that a reference to reconnaissance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: "Reconnaissance call sign were stopped at a well manned BiH" -- CP for checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: "Reconnaissance call signs were stopped at a well manned BiH checkpoint at grid reference 214959. There were approximately 30 to 40 well equipped BiH soldiers armed with RPG-7s whose commander (a woman) stated that", that is the end of that paragraph. Then turning your attention to the second page, at the top: "Reconnaissance call sign reported that the two HVO checkpoints north and south of Busovaca have now been collapsed." What would that mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That the two checkpoints that had prevented movement through the town of Busovaca from the period of about 16th April until this day had been removed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: "The BiH have inserted two checkpoints on the route from Kacuni to Kiseljak at grid reference 390803 and", and there is a letter that may be "3" on the next line, "407794. Soldiers at the latter grid placed a RPG-7 in the fire position and pointed it at a reconnaissance call sign. The BiH have stated that no UN vehicles will be allowed through these checkpoints for the next ten to fifteen days." Does this portion of the Mil Info Summ indicate that the BiH was putting additional pressure on Kiseljak from the direction of Kacuni?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What it refers to is the 24 hour period after the signing of the cease-fire agreement on the 21st April, when General Halilovic came back and asked for an additional 24 hours, because due to the spacing of his forces and the fact that they had been fighting continuously for the last three days, it would require his personal intervention on the field of battle to actually bring the fighting to an end with the BiH forces, and these reports are consistent with the fighting that the BiH were continuing to do on the early morning of the 22nd because the 3rd Corps had been unable to get their orders down, and we had to put General Halilovic in one of our vehicles and actually take him out to these various places for him to personally give the orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I offer exhibit D66, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: It will be both pages?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, it will have both pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Was the process, Colonel, of containing adherence to the cease-fire, was it a process that continued over a number of days after 22nd April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was. There continued to be fighting on both sides sporadically at the tactical level over the next few days, which we interdicted. The most difficult area to actually bring the fighting to an end was in the Kiseljak valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Let me direct your attention to the third document, marked for identification as D67, which is titled in handwritten form, "Cheshire Mil Info 180 28 April 93". I will read it: "Warrior call sign patrolling in the Busovaca/Kiseljak road reported that there was heavy fighting in the area of Kazagici, grid reference 6279, with the village now under the control of the BiH. The HVO had occupied positions around the village yesterday, see Mil Info Summ number 179. However, the BiH appeared to have retaken Kazagici over the last 24 hours. The village was reported to be extremely badly damaged, with almost every house having been set fire to. The central operations group commander, Colonel Blaskic, demanded that BritBat should try harder in their peacekeeping efforts this morning." Is this report consistent with the other reports you were receiving at the time concerning the difficulty of enforcing the cease-fire agreement of 21 April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was continued fighting between HVO and BiH in the Kiseljak valley, especially over contested villages, which was a fall-out from fighting going even as far back as January. We also asked, I remember distinctly, because this message rather annoyed me from Colonel Blaskic, that he also redouble his efforts along with our own to stop his fighting and we said the same to the BiH.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Would you agree that where a village had been taken and retaken and perhaps retaken again by opposing military forces, at the end of that process of fighting, the village is likely to be very heavily damaged?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would certainly think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Is that reflected here in this report concerning Kazagici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have memories of the destruction of Kazagici, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I offer D67, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Colonel, I have had placed on the easel a white tablet of paper and I would like to ask you some questions and then make certain notations on the chart. I will ask you if they are fair and accurate, to help us and the court understand the number of levels of command from the level of the operative zone to that of actual fighting units who would have taken part in the fighting, for example, on 16th April 1993. May I approach the tablet, your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Go ahead, and if the Prosecution wishes to go over to the easel, please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I have one comment. Is Mr. Hayman planning on doing the writing?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Well, we have tried all kinds of things. Sometimes it is the Defence writing, sometimes the Prosecution writing. Mr. Hayman, what do you have in store for us now? Are you going to be doing the drawing or writing, the different command levels?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: There are a number of levels, your Honour. I would like to elicit from the witness what the names of those levels are and then I will simply write and repeat the names of those levels on top of each other on the tablet. I think that is the most efficient way to proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Are you the one who is actually going to do the writing?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I propose to, yes, your Honour. I think that is the most efficient way to proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: It would have perhaps been more efficient if you had prepared a document on which you would have listed what in your opinion represents the chain of command, which would have been put on the ELMO and we could have asked the witness to make his comments about it. Now we are going to see you drawing and writing for a little while, which is not unpleasant, but it is going to waste some time. All right, you could not have done it any other way. Have it put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this point I would object to Mr. Hayman writing anything and if this is going to be some type of exhibit that Mr. Hayman intends to use, let the Colonel do the writing and not counsel.
